newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds lower, yield spreads tighten.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds lower, yield spreads tighten.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities prices dipped on Thursday, but pass-through yield spreads narrowed by a few ticks to Treasuries, traders said.
"Spreads have tightened up a bit in pass-throughs, but that has not been the case for CMOs (collateralized mortgage obligations)," said one trader at a New York investment firm.
He said the CMO market is still digesting Wednesday's bid lists and dealers have been trying to push the new-issue paper out the door, causing yield spreads to widen.
By 1515 EST/2015 GMT, mortgage-backeds were 1/32 to 5/32 lower in premium coupons while discount coupons fell 6/32 to 7/32.
In key coupons, Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5 percent paper was off 6/32 at 100-17/32, yielding 112 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac paper was off 6/32 as well, at 100-11/32 and 100-16/32, respectively.
The 10-year Treasury note was down 13/32 at 99-04/32 to yield 6.37 percent.
Traders said overall the market is in relatively "good" technical shape.

"There are some real supply issues," said one. "Anything that is reasonably well-structured at this point, particularly on collateral that is moderately seasoned, is starting to trade better and better," he said.
